description: The chat language metrics (PL.core-chat-language-metrics, U110(4) Q3): a line's words and target words, the heard grammar checks, targetPercent, the quest's usages, and a chat's lines fed to recordTurn and its end to recordConversation (src/language-learning/chat-metrics.ts).
comparison: exact, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent); an unknown op or step is an error, never a skip

cases.name: words: a target word is a book word after its edge punctuation is stripped, in lower case; every token is a word
cases.note: totalWords = line.trim().split(/\s+/), punctuation-only tokens included (the reference); a token counts as a target word when its chatKey (edge punctuation stripped, lower case) is a book word's, every time it occurs; wordsUsed once each, spelled as the book spells it. A row filed under another language still counts; a phrase matches no single token; an empty line has no words.

cases.name: words: the world language's words count as well; a book row's spelling comes before a world word's
cases.note: worldWords are the language's sample words the host passes (the reference's sampleWords); a word whose key is empty ("...") matches nothing.

cases.name: words: an empty book and no world words: no line has a target word
words: Cyrillic target words count, edge punctuation stripped and in lower case
cases.note: chatKey strips the characters at a token's edges that are not a letter, a combining mark, a digit or _ of any script, then lower-cases: "Привет," is "привет", "ХЛЕБ" and «Хлеб» are "хлеб" (spelled as the book spells it, "Хлеб"). A near miss, a non-book word, a book word with a digit or _ at its edge (digits and _ are word characters, as \w has them) and a dash or dots are words but not target words.

cases.name: words: Greek target words count (case folded, accents kept)
words: Arabic target words count (the Arabic comma and question mark stripped)
words: Hebrew target words count
words: Devanagari target words count (a word ending in a vowel sign keeps it; the danda is stripped)
cases.note: नमस्ते ends in a combining vowel sign (U+0947, a mark), which chatKey keeps, so नमस्त (no vowel sign) is another word; the danda (।, U+0964) is punctuation and is stripped.

cases.name: words: Hangul target words count
percent: min(100, floor(unique words used × 50 / turns)), 0 with no turns
cases.note: Floored to a whole percent, so the 50 and 80 thresholds of the fluency gain decide as the exact ratio does: 19/12 is 79 (79.17), 16/10 is 80, 8/5 is 80; 3 words in one turn is 150, clamped to 100.

cases.name: hear: correct is one right line, corrected adds errorCount (the errors' length when absent), no_target_language nothing
cases.note: grammarChecked = errors + correct lines (the tracker's getConversationGrammarCounts); a corrected check counts its errors, not one per line; a no_target_language check counts nothing, whatever it carries.

cases.name: usages: a line's target words as the quest's useVocabulary usages, quest words first
cases.note: The player's line only, its tokens keyed by chatKey (edge punctuation stripped, lower case): a quest word (spelled as the quest spells it), a book word or a world word; once each, in the line's order, usedCorrectly true. English and near misses are not usages.

lines: Bonjour! Un croissant et du PAIN, pain.
hello there, the bakery is lovely

expected.line: Bonjour! Un croissant et du PAIN, pain.
hello there, the bakery is lovely

cases.name: usages: no quest words: the book's and the world's words only
usages: Cyrillic quest and book words are usages, spelled as the quest spells them
run: Ada's four-line chat, its checks heard after each line, ended into recordConversation (Good grammar, a good mix)
cases.note: Each line's metrics carry the checks heard before it (a line's own check comes with the NPC's answer). Three right lines and one with an error: 30 ≥ 24 but not 36, "Good grammar!". Four words over four turns: targetPercent 50. The words used are active uses in the book.

cases.name: run: an empty line is refused and is not a turn; a chat of no turns ends refused (no free fluency)
run: a chat begun again before the last ended starts at none; world words used are learned
cases.note: Bram's chat is left open and Cora's starts: its turns, words and checks start at none. Cora's words (two world words) are new to the book: wordsLearned 2, each now a row with one active use. No check heard: core's gain reads it as perfect.

cases.name: run: Olga's Russian chat: Cyrillic words used are target words, targetPercent 50, active uses in the book
cases.note: Two book words (привет, Хлеб) over two turns: targetPercent 50, both reinforced (no word learned): each now has one active use. Each line has a target word, so neither turn reads as a struggle on target words.

cases.name: run: three lines of eight target words stretch; sixteen words over three turns clamp at 100 (full immersion)

steps.text: bonjour pain merci maison croissant beurre lait sucre
Farine, four, table, chaise, porte, rue, ville, marché!
pain pain pain pain pain pain pain pain

adjustment.reason: Player is performing exceptionally well — increasing complexity.

cases.name: run: English lines with errors heard scaffold on the second struggling line; no target word, no grammar bonus
cases.note: Line 1 has no check heard yet (struggle 500); two errors heard make line 2's grammar signal 1000 (800); line 3 (3 of 3) is the second high turn and scaffolds. targetPercent 0; grammarCorrect 0 of 3: no grammar bonus.

adjustment.reason: Player is struggling: high grammar error rate, low target language usage, very short responses. Activating scaffolding.
